title: LDL Cholesterol: When Dividing by Five Fails
summary: Calculate LDL-C with the Friedewald equation, see exactly when its TG ÷ 5 assumption breaks (high or non-fasting triglycerides, low LDL-C, type III), and choose non-HDL-C, Sampson–NIH, Martin–Hopkins or apoB instead.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 18 Hit 1 (core: Friedewald and its 400 mg/dL limit), Hit 6 (Martin–Hopkins at low LDL-C; type III overestimation), Hit 17 (non-HDL-C needs no TG term), Traps 1 and 2 and the Figure 18 anchor. Checked against Wolska 2026, Islam 2022 and Kenkre 2025 (HEART UK/ACB). The reviewer’s claim that a direct LDL assay “stays valid even at TG 600” is contradicted — register flag rv-direct-ldl.

objectives: Calculate LDL-C with the Friedewald equation and explain the TG ÷ 5 assumption.
Identify when Friedewald under- or overestimates LDL-C (TG > 400, non-fasting, low LDL-C, type III).
Choose appropriate alternatives: non-HDL-C, Sampson–NIH, Martin–Hopkins, apoB — and know the limits of direct LDL-C assays.

scenes.title: Why the lab refused to calculate LDL
scenes.altText: Two lipid reports side by side. Report 1: TC 240, HDL-C 50, TG 180 → LDL-C 154 (calculated). Report 2: TC 265, HDL-C 42, TG 520 → “LDL-C not calculated”. A question asks why the second one is blank.

cues.text: Two lipid panels. The first has a calculated LDL cholesterol.
The second, with triglycerides of 520, says: LDL cholesterol not calculated.
The lab didn’t forget. The usual LDL formula breaks when triglycerides are high.

props.label: When does the LDL formula fail?

scenes.title: Normal: Friedewald’s subtraction
scenes.altText: A stacked bar of total cholesterol split into HDL-C, LDL-C and VLDL-C. Total cholesterol and HDL-C are measured; VLDL-C is estimated as TG ÷ 5 (mg/dL), because in a fasting sample VLDL carries roughly five times as much triglyceride as cholesterol. Worked example: 240 − 50 − 180/5 = 154 mg/dL.

cues.text: Total cholesterol is spread across lipoproteins. In a fasting sample, it’s mostly HDL, LDL and VLDL cholesterol.
The lab measures total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol and triglycerides. LDL is usually calculated, not measured.
Friedewald’s trick: in fasting blood, VLDL carries about five times more triglyceride than cholesterol. So VLDL cholesterol is estimated as triglycerides divided by five.
Then LDL equals total cholesterol minus HDL minus triglycerides over five. For 240, 50 and 180, that’s 240 minus 50 minus 36: 154 milligrams per decilitre.

scenes.title: What changes: when TG ÷ 5 stops being true
scenes.altText: Four cards light up where the fixed ÷5 assumption breaks. 1 Triglycerides > 400 mg/dL: large TG-rich VLDL carry far more TG per cholesterol, so TG/5 overestimates VLDL-C and LDL-C is underestimated. 2 Non-fasting samples: chylomicrons (mostly TG) inflate TG. 3 Low LDL-C (e.g. < 70 mg/dL): small errors in VLDL-C become large relative errors — underestimation. 4 Type III dysbetalipoproteinemia: cholesterol-rich VLDL (β-VLDL) — TG/5 underestimates VLDL-C, so LDL-C is overestimated.

cues.text: When triglycerides climb above about 400, the VLDL particles get big and triglyceride-rich. Triglycerides over five now overestimates VLDL cholesterol, so calculated LDL comes out too low.
Non-fasting samples add chylomicrons, which are mostly triglyceride. Same problem.
At very low LDL — around 70 or less — a small error in VLDL becomes a big share of the answer, and Friedewald tends to underestimate LDL.
And in type three dysbetalipoproteinaemia, the VLDL is cholesterol-rich. Triglycerides over five now underestimates VLDL cholesterol, so calculated LDL comes out too high.

scenes.title: In the lab: better estimates and safer numbers
scenes.altText: Option cards. Martin–Hopkins: replaces ÷5 with an adjustable factor from TG and non-HDL-C; recommended by guidelines for LDL-C < 70 mg/dL; extended version to TG 800. Sampson–NIH: a multivariable equation built against beta-quantification, usable to TG 800 mg/dL and in non-fasting samples. Non-HDL-C = TC − HDL-C: no TG term, usable non-fasting (e.g. 265 − 42 = 223 mg/dL). ApoB counts atherogenic particles. Caution card: direct (homogeneous) LDL-C assays are method-dependent and can be biased in dyslipidemic, high-TG samples; HEART UK/ACB does not recommend them in hypertriglyceridaemia and suggests apoB. Reference method: beta-quantification (ultracentrifugation).

cues.text: Newer equations fix the five. Martin–Hopkins uses an adjustable factor based on triglycerides and non-HDL cholesterol, and guidelines recommend it when LDL is below 70.
The Sampson–NIH equation was built against the reference method and works up to triglycerides of 800, even non-fasting.
Non-HDL cholesterol is total minus HDL — no triglyceride term at all. For report two: 265 minus 42 is 223. Apolipoprotein B counts the atherogenic particles directly.

Direct LDL assays sound like the answer, but they vary by method and can be biased in high-triglyceride samples. UK guidance prefers apo B there. The true reference is beta-quantification by ultracentrifugation.

props.title: Caution: direct LDL-C assays
lines: Method-dependent; can be biased in high-TG samples

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Trap card: “Calculate Friedewald LDL at TG 550” is crossed out → “Don’t — report non-HDL-C, or use Sampson–NIH / extended Martin–Hopkins.” Trap card: “High Friedewald LDL in type III = intensify for LDL” is crossed out → “β-VLDL makes Friedewald overestimate LDL-C.” Trap card: “A direct LDL is always valid at high TG” is crossed out → “Method-dependent and can be biased; apoB or non-HDL-C are safer.”

cues.text: Trap one: never use Friedewald above 400. Report non-HDL cholesterol, or use an equation validated for higher triglycerides.
Trap two: in type three dysbetalipoproteinaemia, a high calculated LDL is partly remnant cholesterol. Friedewald overestimates it.
Trap three: a direct LDL isn’t automatically valid when triglycerides are high. It depends on the method and can be biased.

props.title: ✗ “Calculate Friedewald LDL at TG 550.”
lines: ✓ Report non-HDL-C, or use Sampson–NIH / extended Martin–Hopkins

props.title: ✗ “Type III: high Friedewald LDL is true LDL.”
✗ “A direct LDL is always valid at high TG.”

scenes.title: Five only works when VLDL behaves
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Divide by five only when VLDL behaves: fasting, TG ≤ 400, LDL not tiny, not type III.” And “Non-HDL never needs the five.” A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: divide by five only when VLDL behaves — fasting, triglycerides under 400, LDL not tiny, and not type three. Non-HDL never needs the five.

Where it breaks: in millimoles per litre the divisor is about 2.2, not 5; guidelines differ between countries on which equation to use; equations aren’t validated above about 800; and a lab’s chosen method decides what it reports.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: mmol/L divisor ≈ 2.2 · guidelines differ by country
Equations not validated above ~800 mg/dL · local method decides

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Friedewald LDL-C = TC − HDL-C − TG/5: fasting, TG ≤ 400 only”, “Above that (or LDL < 70, type III): non-HDL-C, Sampson–NIH, Martin–Hopkins, apoB”.

cues.text: Friedewald’s LDL works only in fasting samples with triglycerides up to 400 — otherwise report non-HDL cholesterol or use a newer equation or apo B, and remember type III makes it read high.

props.label: LDL-C = TC − HDL-C − TG/5 · fasting, TG ≤ 400 only

explanation.what: Plain language: labs usually work out LDL “bad” cholesterol by subtraction, using a shortcut for the cholesterol in VLDL that only holds under normal conditions. Scientific terms: Friedewald LDL-C = TC − HDL-C − TG/5 (mg/dL), with VLDL-C estimated from a fixed TG:VLDL-C ratio of 5 in fasting samples.
explanation.why: Hypertriglyceridaemia and non-fasting samples raise the TG:cholesterol ratio of TG-rich lipoproteins, so TG/5 overestimates VLDL-C and LDL-C is underestimated; at low LDL-C, VLDL-C errors are proportionally larger; in type III dysbetalipoproteinaemia, cholesterol-enriched β-VLDL makes TG/5 too small and LDL-C is overestimated.
explanation.measure: Do not use Friedewald when TG > 400 mg/dL. Martin–Hopkins (adjustable factor) is recommended for LDL-C < 70 mg/dL (TG ≤ 400; extended version to 800). Sampson–NIH (derived against beta-quantification) to TG 800 mg/dL and usable non-fasting. Non-HDL-C = TC − HDL-C, usable non-fasting. ApoB reflects atherogenic particle number. Direct LDL-C assays are method-dependent and can be biased in dyslipidaemic samples; HEART UK/ACB does not recommend them in hypertriglyceridaemia. Reference method: beta-quantification.
explanation.differs: Calculated (Friedewald, Martin–Hopkins, Sampson–NIH) vs measured (direct homogeneous, beta-quantification) LDL-C; LDL-C vs non-HDL-C vs apoB.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: a Friedewald calculation, the 400 mg/dL limit, what to report instead, non-HDL-C arithmetic, and the type III overestimation trap.

comparisons.title: Friedewald vs newer equations

left.label: Friedewald
points: Fasting; TG ≤ 400; inaccurate at low LDL-C

right.label: Martin–Hopkins / Sampson–NIH
points: Better at low LDL-C; up to TG 800 (Sampson, extended M–H)

comparisons.distinguisher: Whether the TG:VLDL-C ratio is fixed or adapts to the sample.

comparisons.title: Non-HDL-C vs direct LDL-C at high TG

right.label: Direct LDL-C
points: Can be biased in high-TG samples

comparisons.distinguisher: Non-HDL-C relies only on two well-standardised measurements.

mnemonic.text: Divide by five only when VLDL behaves: fasting, TG ≤ 400, LDL not tiny, not type III — and non-HDL never needs the five.
mnemonic.explanation: Each condition protects the fixed TG:VLDL-C ratio that Friedewald depends on; non-HDL-C avoids triglycerides entirely.
mnemonic.limitation: In mmol/L the divisor is about 2.2; guidelines differ by country; equations are not validated above ~800 mg/dL; the laboratory’s method determines what is reported.

takeaway: Friedewald’s LDL works only in fasting samples with triglycerides up to 400 — otherwise report non-HDL cholesterol or use a newer equation or apo B, and remember type III makes it read high.

questions.stem: Total cholesterol 240 mg/dL, HDL-C 50 mg/dL, triglycerides 180 mg/dL (fasting). What is the Friedewald LDL-C?

options.rationale: Incorrect. That is non-HDL-C (240 − 50), without subtracting VLDL-C.
Incorrect. The full triglyceride value was subtracted instead of TG/5.
Incorrect. HDL-C must be subtracted, not TG/5 added.

questions.stem: TC 265 mg/dL, HDL-C 42 mg/dL, TG 520 mg/dL. Which LDL-related value can be validly reported from these results?

options.rationale: Correct. Non-HDL-C (TC − HDL-C) has no triglyceride term and stays valid at high TG.
Incorrect. Friedewald should not be used above TG 400 mg/dL.
Incorrect. TG/5 is unreliable at this triglyceride level.
Incorrect. Non-HDL-C can be reported now.

questions.stem: In type III dysbetalipoproteinaemia, how does the Friedewald equation behave?

options.text: It overestimates LDL-C because cholesterol-rich β-VLDL makes TG/5 too small
options.rationale: Correct. VLDL-C is underestimated, so the remainder assigned to LDL-C is too large.

options.text: It underestimates LDL-C, as in ordinary hypertriglyceridaemia
options.rationale: Incorrect. That pattern applies to TG-rich VLDL, not cholesterol-rich β-VLDL.

options.text: It is exact because TG and cholesterol rise equally
options.rationale: Incorrect. Equal rises do not make the TG:VLDL-C ratio equal to 5.

options.text: It cannot be calculated because HDL-C is zero
options.rationale: Incorrect. HDL-C is not absent in type III.

High/non-fasting TG → LDL-C underestimated; low LDL-C → underestimated; type III → overestimated.
Martin–Hopkins for LDL-C < 70; Sampson–NIH to TG 800 and non-fasting; non-HDL-C = TC − HDL-C usable non-fasting; apoB; beta-quantification reference method.
Direct LDL-C assays are method-dependent and can be biased in dyslipidaemic/high-TG samples; HEART UK/ACB does not recommend them in hypertriglyceridaemia.
